resources.string: No serial adapter found. Plug in a USB console cable or a USB-to-serial adapter - through an OTG adapter if the phone has only USB-C. Supported: FTDI, Prolific PL2303, Silicon Labs CP210x, WCH CH34x, and CDC/ACM devices, which includes the USB console port on Cisco equipment.
This device does not support USB host mode, so it cannot drive a USB serial adapter.
Android asks for permission to use it when you connect.
Access to the adapter was not granted. Connect again and allow it in the system dialog.
The adapter could not be opened. Another app may be using it.
The adapter refused these line settings - most often a baud rate it cannot do.
The connection to the adapter was lost.
The terminal component could not be loaded on this device.
%1$d lines will be sent as commands, one every %2$d ms. The device executes each line as it arrives.
This adapter does not support that flow control. None is used.
The session log could not be written.
Changes apply to an open session immediately. If the console shows garbage, the baud rate is almost always the cause.
CR is right for practically all network equipment. Change it only if a device ignores your commands.
Asserted by default; some devices only talk once DTR is up. Switch off for boards that reset on DTR, such as an Arduino.
Network equipment echoes what you type. Switch this on only if your keystrokes do not appear.
A device reads characters faster than it runs commands. Pasted too fast, lines are dropped without any error message.
Keep the screen on while connected
Record the session to a file

Saved under Console-Logs in the file server\'s share, so it can be fetched over SFTP or FTP right away. A console capture often contains configuration with password hashes - which is why this is off by default.
